Set Order of Period Levels for a Reporting Tree

Source: R/period_set_order_tree.R
period_set_order_tree.Rd

Modify the levels attribute of labels so that periods are ordered as a reporting tree: the most detailed periods first, then broader periods, then period not stated.

Usage

period_set_order_tree(
  labels,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"),
  x_arg = rlang::caller_arg(labels),
  call = rlang::current_env()
)

Arguments

labels

Vector of period labels.

interpret_single

How to interpret a label for a single year, such as "2020". Choices are "lower" (the default) and "upper". See below for details.

interpret_multi

How to interpret a label that refers to multiple years, such as "2020-2025". Choices are NULL (the default), "at_upper", and "below_upper". See below for details.

interpret_fail

Action if element of labels cannot be interpreted. Choices are "error" (the default), "warn", and "silent".

x_arg

Name of labels to use in error and warning messages. Defaults to the expression supplied for labels. A function that calls this function can supply its own name, such as "data$age".

call

Execution environment of the function to name in error and warning messages. The default is this function itself. A function that calls this function can supply call = rlang::current_env(), so that messages name it instead.

Value

Factor with the same length as labels.

Details

In a reporting tree, periods nest: any two periods either do not overlap, or one contains the other. Reporting trees arise, for instance, in census tables of year of arrival, where most records have detailed periods ("2015-2020"), some have only broad periods ("<2010"), and some have no period at all ("Missing").

Levels are ordered as follows:

  1. Leaves, that is, periods that contain no other period, ordered by lower limit.

  2. Broader periods, ordered so that each period comes after all periods inside it, and before any period entirely above it.

  3. Labels that could not be interpreted, if interpret_fail is "warn" or "silent".

  4. Labels for missing values, as defined by period_is_missing().

Different labels that describe the same period are placed next to each other, in the order in which they first appear. Leaves do not need to lie at the same depth in the tree.

period_set_order_tree() checks only that the periods nest. It does not check, for instance, that the leaves cover the full span. Labels for totals, as defined by period_is_total(), are not part of a reporting tree, and cause an error. Some tables use "Total" to mean period not stated. In such cases, recode the total to "Missing" before calling period_set_order_tree(), for instance using x[period_is_total(x)] <- "Missing".

period_set_order_tree() has no effect on the values of labels. Only the levels are changed.

Rules for interpreting inputs

Single-year

Labels for single-year periods sometimes refer to the lower limits of periods, and sometimes refer to upper limits. For instance, the label "2020" is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2021, and is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 July 2019 and ends at midnight on 1 July 2020.

The interpret_single argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_singleRuleExample
"lower""a" -> [a,a+1)"2020" -> [2020,2021)
"upper""a" -> [a-1,a)"2020" -> [2019,2020)

Multi-year

In labels for multi-year periods, the second number is sometimes the upper limit of the period, and sometimes the upper limit minus 1. For instance, the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2025 is sometimes labelled "2020-2025" and is sometimes labelled "2020-2024".

The interpret_multi argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_multiRuleExample
"at_upper""a-b" -> [a,b)"2020-2025" -> [2020,2025)
"below_upper""a-b" -> [a,b+1)"2020-2024" -> [2020,2025)

If interpret_multi is NULL (the default), then multi-year labels are interpreted using the "at_upper" convention. If, however, the "at_upper" convention leads to intervals with widths 4, 9, 14, ..., then agetime emits a message. Supplying an explicit value for interpret_multi silences this message.

Open

A period that is open on the left has no lower limit, and a period that is open on the right has no upper limit. Labels for open periods are not affected by interpret_single or interpret_multi.

Some examples of open periods:

LabelInterval
"<2000", "before 2000", "under 2000"(-Inf,2000)
"2000 or earlier", "up to 2000"(-Inf,2001)
"2000+", "2000 or more", "2000 or later"[2000,Inf)

Labels starting with "-", such as "-2000", are not accepted.

See also

  • period_set_order() Order periods by lower limit

  • age_set_order_tree() Age equivalent of period_set_order_tree()

  • cohort_set_order_tree() Cohort equivalent of period_set_order_tree()

Examples

## year of arrival: detailed periods, arrival
## known only as before 2010, and not stated
labels <- c("2015-2020", "2010-2015", "<2000", "2000-2010",
            "<2010", "Missing")
period_set_order_tree(labels)
#> [1] 2015-2020 2010-2015 <2000     2000-2010 <2010     Missing  
#> Levels: <2000 2000-2010 2010-2015 2015-2020 <2010 Missing
